overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session on April 3 under Purpose 6 for an improper purpose, and ordered future compliance plus release of the April 3 executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: The Commission entered executive session on April 3 under Purpose 6 (real property) for an improper purpose, without the chair declaring that an open meeting may harm its negotiating position.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the Commission entered executive session for an improper purpose.

allegations.summary: During the executive session, the Commission discussed a grant for appraisal and site plans, which is outside the narrow scope of Purpose 6.
allegations.key_passage: Discussion of a grant and sensitivity to property owners’ desire for secrecy do not fall within the narrow permissible scope of a Purpose 6 discussion.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Release the April 3 executive session minutes to the public in their entirety and without redactions, and certify within 30 days of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law. In addition, we order the Commission to release to the public the minutes of the April 3 executive session, in their entirety and without redactions, and to certify that it has done so within 30 days of the date of this letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
